ui_bugs.issue: After clicking 'Start Exam' on the Mock Exam start page, the exam page (/module/{moduleId}/mock-exam) is stuck on the loading spinner indefinitely. Verified via DOM inspection: main element still renders the `if (loading)` fallback (Loader2 at lines 151-156) 12s+ after mount, even though POST /api/mock-exams/{id}/start returns 200 with attempt_id and GET /api/mock-exams/{id} returns 200 with 3 questions. Users cannot access questions/timer/submit — the whole exam-taking flow is unreachable through the UI.

Continue Learning points to MODULE 18 (AI 101 for Non-Tech Analysts) instead of Module 16's Mock Exam as specified in the review request. Root cause: the seed script marked user_modules.is_completed=TRUE for M16 in addition to marking all 15 sessions complete, so the next-actionable-module algorithm treats M16 as fully done and jumps to M18. Review request explicitly stated 'module 16 itself (user_modules.is_completed) was deliberately left FALSE so the mock exam is the next actionable step' — actual DB state contradicts this. Not a code bug — a seed-data bug in the previous turn's DB seeding.

integration_issues.issue: Cannot proceed past Start Exam click — MockExamPage never leaves loading state. Backend flow (start→get→submit) is fully working (proven by pytest 6/6). Something in MockExamPage's useEffect load() closure or state-setter is not flipping `loading` to false in practice, despite the fetch succeeding. Likely candidates: (a) `mounted` cleanup in StrictMode double-invocation causing the first-run setLoading(false) to be skipped and the second-run to also be skipped if user?.id or attemptId flips, (b) the initial `if (!user?.id) { setLoading(false); return; }` early-exit followed by a re-run where `attemptId` from location.state has already been consumed/nulled by react-router — check whether location.state survives StrictMode double-mount; if it doesn't, the `if (!attemptId) navigate(...start...)` may fire but not actually change URL because /mock-exam/start was already the referrer with replace:true → potential redirect loop hiding as 'still loading'. Recommend: add a `data-testid='mock-exam-page-loading'` on the loader for observability, add console.log/error boundaries in the load() try/catch, and consider passing attempt_id via URL query param instead of react-router state so a page refresh / StrictMode re-mount doesn't lose it.

critical_code_review_comments: MockExamPage.jsx line 74: `if (!user?.id) { setLoading(false); return; }` inside the effect's load() function doesn't restore setLoading(true) on the next re-run — it works but is fragile. Combined with the `if (!attemptId) navigate(...)` on the next line (which does NOT set loading), any transient state where attemptId is undefined mid-render can wedge the UI. Recommend using a state machine (idle | loading | ready | error) instead of a bare boolean.

MockExamPage.jsx: attempt_id is passed only via `location.state`. If the user hits F5 / a react-router remount drops state, the page silently redirects to /start losing the started attempt on the server. Recommend passing attempt_id as a URL search param (?attempt=uuid) so it survives reloads.

wave_endpoints.py exam endpoints exist and are solid, but there's no session-count-based gating check on /api/mock-exams/{module_id}/start — a user with 0 sessions complete can still start the exam. Not necessarily a bug (product may allow this), but worth confirming the product intent.
MockExamStartPage.jsx: 'Back to Module' link goes to `/module/{moduleId}/project/start`, but /module/{id} itself is 404 — inconsistent module-detail navigation. Consider a canonical module route.

rca of the issue: MockExamPage.jsx load() effect: on first mount, user may be null (auth still resolving) → early setLoading(false) return. When user populates, effect re-runs; setLoading(true) then load() proceeds. However, in React StrictMode dev mode + react-router-dom v6, `location.state` from navigate(state:{}) is preserved across the double-invocation, but the effect's cleanup fires between runs and closes the `mounted` var. In the second run, if the API succeeds we should setLoading(false). We CONFIRMED the API returns 200 with 3 questions (both from external pytest and from browser Network panel showing 200 responses). Yet DOM shows `main` element with `x-line-number='151'` (the loading branch) persistently — meaning React's `loading` state is still true. This suggests either (a) an unhandled promise rejection between the fetch success and setState, (b) a stale-closure bug where the setLoading call fires but the state has been reset by a subsequent re-render, or (c) attemptId is undefined on the effect that actually completes, and the navigate(...) fallback silently no-ops because we're already at /mock-exam (react-router replace:true to /start followed by return — this returns from load() WITHOUT calling setLoading(false)). Most likely (c) — see line 75. Reproduction: login as nism.tester, go to /module/5a6dd7bb-.../mock-exam/start, click Start Exam. Observe URL becomes /module/{id}/mock-exam and spinner spins forever. Mitigation: (i) always setLoading(false) in the attemptId-missing branch and/or use a state-machine, (ii) also pass attempt_id via URL search param so refresh/remount doesn't drop it.
